title: Distance Teaching Experience of Campus-based Teachers at Times of Pandemic Confinement
venue: ACM 5th International Conference on Education Technology Management (ICETM 2022)
extended_summary:
This paper examines how campus-based university teachers experienced the sudden shift to distance teaching during COVID-19 pandemic confinement. The authors were interested in the practical challenges teachers faced, how they adapted their teaching, what they learned from the experience, and whether those lessons might improve future campus-based teaching after the pandemic.

The study is based on online, semi-structured interviews with six teachers from the Computer Science department at Blekinge Institute of Technology in Sweden. The interview prompts focused on adaptation, session recording, Zoom fatigue, virtual reality, and lessons learned. The authors then applied inductive qualitative thematic analysis to the transcripts. The paper is therefore about teacher perceptions and reflections rather than a tested coaching or generative AI intervention.

The main findings were that interaction with students was much harder online, especially when webcams were off and nonverbal cues were missing. Teachers valued asynchronous communication tools such as chat, polls, Kahoot, Mentimeter, and Padlet because these reduced shyness barriers and sometimes increased participation. Recorded lectures were widely seen as useful for flexibility and review, but they also reduced opportunities for live questioning and could promote procrastination. Teachers reported increased workload, technical strain, and Zoom fatigue, but many expected to keep some online elements, especially hybrid or flipped approaches, in future campus teaching.

identified_tools.description: A generic AI system or chatbot based on generative AI/LLM capabilities; no specific commercial or research product is named in the paper.
identified_tools.use_case: Not actually studied as an AI tool. The paper discusses distance teaching during COVID-19 and mentions digital tools such as Zoom, polls, Mentimeter, Kahoot, Padlet, and Discord, but no generative AI coaching system for teachers.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study, but it does not evaluate an AI tool or teacher-coaching system. The paper provides contextual findings about remote teaching practices rather than evidence for generative AI coaching.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI intervention effect is reported, so there is no measurable impact on teacher uptake or reflective practice attributable to a tool. The paper only suggests general digital tools for engagement.
